jobs.description:
Company Overview

Moss is a national privately held construction firm providing innovative solutions resulting in award-winning projects. With regional offices across the United States, Moss focuses on construction management, solar EPC, design-build, and public-private partnerships. The company’s diverse portfolio encompasses a wide range of sectors, including luxury high-rise residential, landmark mixed-use developments, hospitality, K-12 and higher education, justice, solar energy and battery storage, and sports. Moss is ranked by Engineering News-Record as one of the nation’s top 65 general contractors, and the 3rd ranked solar EPC nationwide. Moss prides itself on a strong entrepreneurial culture that honors safety, quality, client engagement and employee development. Its employees consistently rank Moss as one of the best places to work.

POSITION SCOPE AND ORGANIZATIONAL IMPACT

The Solar Director of Preconstruction and Engineering
provides leadership for preconstruction, estimating, and engineering functions to support the Solar Division in the pursuit and execution of large utility-scale solar projects
based out of the Hawaii Office
. This role drives accuracy and consistency in estimating, oversight of engineering deliverables, team development, and collaboration with owners, consultants, trade contractors, and vendors to support successful project pursuits and transitions to operations.

Essential Job Duties And Responsibilities

Lead and manage the preconstruction and engineering effort for utility-scale solar projects, from early-stage concept through final contract pricing and handoff.
Manage the estimating process for EPC, conceptual/schematic, and various stages of progress construction drawings through final contract pricing for the solar industry.
Produce estimate summaries indicating project costs and margin potential, while supporting conversion to both Owner bid forms and Moss internal budget formats.
Prepare, update, and track estimates as design documents progress, including value engineering analysis and reconciliation of scope, assumptions, and clarifications.
Provide leadership in creating, reviewing, and revising drafts and deliverables for solar utility-scale ground mount projects.
Review, analyze, and provide comments on owner contracts, subcontract agreements, consultant agreements, and other project related contracts to identify commercial, technical, operational, and risk related issues.
Build, train, and manage the preconstruction and engineering team; establish assignments, priorities, and key staff objectives.
Provide training/seminars to the department and promote continuous improvement in estimating, engineering coordination, and preconstruction processes.
Monitor adherence to all departmental processes; correct non-compliance as required.
Conduct department meetings and ensure clear communication of expectations, schedules, and deliverables.
Responsible for all deliverables produced by the department, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and timeliness.
Support and manage relationships with owners, design consultants, vendors, and trade contractors to align with project goals.
Coordinate project handoff to operations teams and ensure all preconstruction, engineering, and contractual information is accurately transferred for successful project execution
Establish and maintain strong business relationships with trade contractors and vendors to ensure support and interest in bidding and executing solar projects.
Provide support to early-stage project management, engineering, and operations teams to enable successful project planning and execution.
Communicate and interact effectively with the project owner, design consultants, and Moss staff to meet project goals.
Provide high-level summaries of bids to the Leadership Team at the time of submission or by the following morning, including key risks, assumptions, and opportunities.
Focus on risk management training and development of systems, standards, constructability, and scope development practices.
Oversee trade contractor compliance and performance expectations (including contractor scorecards) for trade contractors bidding projects.
Review trade contractor applicants who submit information through established channels and/or advise the Vice President of Solar as appropriate.
Provide staff performance reviews and recommend salary adjustments to the Vice President of Solar.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Education And Work Experience

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, electrical engineering, or related discipline preferred.
Minimum 8 years of engineering and management experience, including minimum 5 years supporting utility-scale solar projects.
Strong background in solar utility-scale ground mount projects (engineering coordination, constructability, and preconstruction execution).
Strong estimating and project scheduling background.
Strong computer skills are a necessity (MS Office / Excel / PowerPoint / Word), including familiarity with construction project management applications and estimating software.
Experience with HCSS Heavy Bid, Accubid, MS Project, Primavera, AGTEK, BlueBeam, and InSite Software is an advantage.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills required to interface directly with owners’ representatives, the A/E team, building departments, and other team members.
Ability to read, interpret, and understand plans proficiently; ability to read specifications and understand subject matter.
Ability to perform accurate quantity survey take-offs.
Demonstrated leadership skills, including experience managing and developing teams of estimators, project engineers, and/or engineering staff.

jobs.title: Director, Applications Engineering
jobs.description:
About Ventiva

Ventiva is a leader in active cooling solutions for electronic devices, delivering thinner, faster, and cooler high-performance products that remain lightweight, silent, and vibration-free. Its patented Ionic Cooling Engine (ICE) technology provides an all-electronic heat transfer solution that addresses thermal challenges in modern high-performance semiconductor design. ICE technology generates airflow without moving parts by using electrohydrodynamic (EHD) principles to move ionized air molecules within an electric field. Ventiva’s ICE9 thermal management suite offers smart, adaptive cooling that continuously monitors system needs and adjusts airflow accordingly. By combining advanced monitoring, algorithms, and real-time software, ICE9 supports robust, device-wide thermal management integrated with overall system performance.

About the Role

The Director, Applications Engineering is a full-time, on-site role based in Fremont, CA. This role leads the applications engineering function, guiding the integration of Ventiva’s ICE and ICE9 technologies into customer systems and reference designs. The director collaborates closely with product, software, and hardware teams to define requirements, validate performance, and resolve complex thermal and system-level challenges. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing engineering projects, overseeing customer evaluations and proof-of-concept builds, providing technical leadership to the applications engineering team, and ensuring timely, high-quality delivery of solutions. The role also involves engaging with key customers and partners, supporting pre- and post-sales technical activities, and contributing to product roadmaps and application guidelines based on real-world use cases.

What You'll Own

Demonstrated Team Leadership skills, including mentoring, performance management, and building high-performing, cross-functional engineering teams.
Strong Project Management capabilities to plan, prioritize, and execute multiple applications engineering projects and customer engagements.
Experience in Product Management and Product Development, particularly in defining requirements, influencing roadmaps, and aligning solutions with market and customer needs.
Hands-on Software Development or software integration experience, preferably with embedded systems, device control, or thermal management software.
Relevant technical background in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, thermal management, or a related field; bachelor’s degree required, advanced degree preferred.
Proven experience in applications engineering or customer-facing technical roles within semiconductor, electronics, or hardware-focused companies.
Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including customers and executive leadership.
Track record of working on-site in lab and hardware environments, with familiarity in system testing, validation, and performance characterization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make data-driven decisions and adapt to evolving technologies and customer requirements.

What You'll Bring

12+ years in applications, systems, or platform engineering in notebook, client compute, or semiconductor — mechanical, systems, electrical, or power domain. Thermal depth welcome, not required.
Direct experience carrying an OEM or ODM design engagement from concept to mass production; you know what a qualification gate actually requires.
Fluency across the client compute stack: SoC power/thermal envelopes, board layout constraints, memory topology tradeoffs, and the firmware/system software layer that ties them together.
Track record hiring and running a distributed applications team, including Taiwan/Greater China.
Credibility in the room with a customer VP of Engineering — you can hold an architecture conversation, not just a spec review.
BS/MS in Mechanical, Electrical, or Systems Engineering.

This is a key role for Ventiva. Applications Engineering is not support. It is where the platform argument gets won or lost. The Director of Applications Engineering is the technical author of Ventiva’s credibility with every partner that matters.﻿

Salary Range: $190,000 - $225,000

Sr Director Strategic Platform Execution

Job Summary

The Senior Director, Strategic Platform Execution leads a global organization accountable for bringing TerumoBCT's devices, disposables, and software to market. The role reports to the Senior Vice President, R&D and sits on the R&D Leadership Team. It owns how that work is planned, prioritized, sequenced, and delivered across multiple sites, along with the standards and governance that keep delivery predictable, and it is the senior R&D voice on what TerumoBCT builds and in what order. The Senior Director advises executive leadership on long-range strategy and investment, settles competing priorities, and is accountable for the results that follow, from growth in market share to lower cost and stronger product quality in developed and emerging markets. Much of that gets done through others. The functional engineering teams are peers rather than reports, so the work depends on the frameworks this role sets and on the credibility the leader builds with those teams. The same is true of Commercial, including Enterprise Marketing, where this organization is R&D's chief partner. Together they shape roadmaps, product line strategies, and value propositions, and they run Product Lifecycle Management as a shared process across functions. The Senior Director is accountable for turning what Commercial needs into commitments R&D can meet. Strategic Platform Execution is newly formed, and whoever takes it on will help decide how it is built and how TerumoBCT develops products in the years ahead. We welcome candidates who want that scope.

Is the senior authority and "go to" global leader for platform, program, and project execution across the devices, disposables, and software portfolio, and represents the organization on significant matters with internal and external stakeholders
Owns planning and decision-making for the portfolio, and advises top management on long-range direction for the global platform strategy

Leads the change management and communication that carry cultural change through global R&D, and adjusts the approach based on how well it takes hold
Defines metrics and governance that track operational performance and progress on change, and that reward the way the organization wants to work
Determines the structure and staffing this organization requires, and is responsible for reviewing, evaluating, and developing its leaders and teams while working across a global, cross-functional environment
Works across regional and functional boundaries to meet business objectives and project timelines
Ensures product design and documentation meet FDA and global regulatory requirements, sets standards for technical documentation and product lifecycle management, and leads or sponsors quality system remediation and major quality initiatives

jobs.description:
Job Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

We are seeking an experienced Director, Fuel Cell & Power Generation Operations
to lead the operation, reliability, and continuous improvement of on-site power generation supporting mission-critical data center infrastructure.

This role will have operational responsibility for fuel cell systems serving as a primary source of on-site power
, along with backup and emergency generator systems
and associated electrical and balance-of-plant infrastructure.

A strong understanding of fuel cell technology, operating characteristics, controls, maintenance requirements, and system integration
is critical to success in this role. The Director will establish the teams, operating practices, maintenance strategies, and technical procedures necessary to safely operate these assets while maintaining continuous protection of critical compute load.

The ideal candidate brings leadership experience from fuel cell operations, fuel cell technology or service organizations, mission-critical power operations, or power generation environments with direct fuel cell experience
. This leader will also play a key role in commissioning new generation assets and establishing a scalable operating model as our on-site power generation capabilities grow.

Key Responsibilities

Lead, develop, and scale teams responsible for the operation and maintenance of fuel cell power generation systems, backup and emergency generators, and associated electrical and balance-of-plant infrastructure.
Provide technical and operational leadership for fuel cell systems, including equipment performance, operating characteristics, controls, maintenance requirements, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management.
Establish operating strategies that maximize fuel cell availability, reliability, and performance while ensuring continuous protection of mission-critical compute load.
Develop, document, test, and continuously improve Methods of Procedure (MOPs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Emergency Operating Procedures (EOPs), and maintenance procedures.
Establish procedures to safely manage generation transitions, load transfers, ramp events, equipment outages, utility events, and other normal and abnormal operating conditions.
Partner with engineering, commissioning, data center operations, training, and technology providers to develop effective technical qualification, repair, preventive maintenance, and training programs.
Lead operational readiness, commissioning, acceptance, and turnover of new fuel cell generation assets and associated electrical infrastructure.
Develop maintenance strategies using equipment condition, operating history, manufacturer requirements, and performance data to maximize generation availability and reliability.
Establish, monitor, and report performance metrics for system availability, reliability, efficiency, equipment health, maintenance effectiveness, and incident response.
Manage operational relationships and agreements with fuel cell technology providers, service organizations, generator providers, utilities, and other critical partners.
Recruit, hire, develop, and retain specialized operations and maintenance personnel with the technical capabilities required to support fuel cell and backup generation systems.
Serve as the senior operational escalation point for high-severity generation incidents, coordinating troubleshooting, recovery, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions.
Champion a culture of safety, operational discipline, compliance, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Maintain knowledge of emerging fuel cell and power generation technologies, operating practices, and regulatory requirements relevant to mission-critical facilities.

Responsibilities

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Energy Systems, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant technical and operational experience.
Significant experience operating, maintaining, commissioning, engineering, or technically supporting fuel cell power generation systems.
Strong working knowledge of fuel cell technology and its application in continuous power generation environments.
Demonstrated understanding of fuel cell operating characteristics, balance-of-plant systems, controls, maintenance practices, failure modes, and equipment performance.
Experience integrating primary generation systems with critical electrical loads and backup/emergency generation.
Demonstrated leadership experience building and developing technical operations, maintenance, field service, or engineering teams.
Experience establishing operating procedures, maintenance programs, technical qualification programs, and operational readiness processes.
Demonstrated ability to lead troubleshooting and operational decision-making in high-availability environments.
Strong safety mindset and experience operating within structured environmental, health, safety, and regulatory requirements.
Strong communication and cross-functional leadership skills with the ability to work effectively across operations, engineering, commissioning, technology providers, utilities, and business organizations.

Highly Relevant Experience

Experience in several of the following areas would be particularly valuable:

Fuel cell technology and power generation
Fuel cell operations and maintenance
Fuel cell field service or technical operations
Fuel cell installation and commissioning
Fuel cell balance-of-plant systems
Natural gas systems supporting fuel cell generation
Generation controls, SCADA, and power monitoring systems
Mission-critical electrical infrastructure
Data center power operations
Backup and emergency generator systems
Commissioning and operational turnover of new power infrastructure
High-availability power generation environments

Preferred Qualifications

Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you’ll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you’ll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

We’re hiring a Director, Supply Chain Engineering to build the systems that take Nscale from demand signal to deployed compute.

This role sits within Corporate Technology and reports to the SVP, Corporate Technology, partnering closely with Data Center and AI Infrastructure teams, as well as Finance, Procurement, and Operations. You’ll design, build, and deploy the systems, platforms, and workflows spanning demand signal, hardware configuration and BOM development, supplier and ODM coordination, logistics and staging, spare inventory management, and more. You won’t run supply chain operations or own procurement—you’ll work alongside those owners and own how the work is represented in software.

Success means this work runs on systems rather than spreadsheets. Teams will work from shared, accurate data, changes will propagate without manual chasing, and routine coordination will be handled through automation and agentic workflows. Your work will directly determine how quickly Nscale can turn hardware into live compute.

Platform Ownership & Roadmap

Own the supply chain technology stack end to end, including strategy, implementation, platform health, configuration, integrations, upgrades, and roadmap planning.
Identify capability gaps and lead the evaluation, procurement, and implementation of new tools.
Build and maintain a templated, repeatable deployment model for supply chain systems across data centers and regions.

Integration & Data Architecture

Define and govern integration architecture across supply chain, finance, procurement, logistics, and infrastructure platforms.
Ensure reliable data exchange and auditability across connected systems.
Collaboratively define the data model and maintain data integrity across platforms.
Design workflows that connect each stage of the supply chain so one team’s output becomes another team’s reliable input.

Automation & Workflow Engineering

Build systems and workflows spanning demand signals, hardware configuration, BOM development, supplier and ODM coordination, logistics, staging, and spare inventory management.
Replace spreadsheet-based processes and manual coordination with scalable systems, automation, and agentic workflows.
Ensure changes propagate across teams and systems without unnecessary manual intervention.

Stakeholder & Vendor Management

Serve as the primary technology partner for supply chain technology across Data Center, AI Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and Operations.
Manage competing demands across teams and regions while maintaining clear priorities and governance.
Own vendor relationships, contract performance, and platform renewals for purchased systems and services, applying a total-cost-of-ownership lens.
Align cross-functional stakeholders around shared standards and scalable ways of working.

KPIs

Accuracy and integrity of cross-platform supply chain data
Reliability of integrations and change propagation
Speed from hardware demand signal to live compute

10+ years of experience in supply chain technology, enterprise systems, or a closely related field

3+ years deploying technology systems across multiple sites or regions
Functional experience with platforms supporting to source-to-contract, BOM management, asset tracking, procure-to-pay platforms, and ERP systems
Experience in data center, hardware infrastructure, or GPU/AI compute supply chains
Proven ability to manage competing stakeholder demands while maintaining clear standards
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced evolving environment

Familiarity with DCIM/IPAM tooling and cross-border hardware logistics
Experience supporting M&A integration or global expansion from a systems perspective

At Nscale, you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and we want you at the core.

Highly competitive US compensation package (base + bonus + equity), with performance reviews every 12 months.

Join one of the fastest-growing AI infrastructure companies — your chance to directly shape how global AI capacity is planned and deployed.

Job Description

The Senior Manager will lead a team of engineers while serving as a hands-on technical leader responsible for defining, building, and operating next-generation AI systems on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This leader will set the architecture and engineering direction for production-grade agentic AI platforms, autonomous workflows, scalable inference infrastructure, and enterprise AI applications used in large-scale, business-critical environments.

This role requires an experienced engineering manager who can build and develop high-performing teams, translate ambiguous product and platform goals into a durable technical strategy, and drive execution across multiple organizations. The successful candidate will be accountable for hiring, mentoring, performance management, technical planning, and delivery, while remaining actively involved in system design, prototyping, coding, code reviews, operational readiness, and incident follow-up.

The ideal candidate combines deep distributed-systems expertise with practical, hands-on experience building AI agents and AI-native applications. This includes developing and orchestrating LLM-based agents, tools, APIs, memory systems, retrieval pipelines, evaluations, guardrails, and cloud-service integrations. The candidate should be comfortable writing production code, debugging complex systems, and guiding engineers through difficult architectural and implementation decisions.

Proven ability to lead teams while remaining technically engaged in design, coding, reviews, debugging, and operations.

Hands-on experience building AI agents, autonomous workflows, tool-using systems, or multi-step orchestration.

Strong Python skills and experience with Kubernetes, Docker, observability, scalability, and fault tolerance.
Strong understanding of AI security, governance, access control, auditability, and operational risk.
Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership skills.

Experience managing teams that build AI platforms, agent runtimes, inference systems, or developer platforms.
Experience with GPU inference optimization, model serving, workflow engines, or multi-tenant cloud services.
Experience integrating AI systems with enterprise APIs, databases, identity systems, vector stores, and policy layers.
Experience with agent evaluation, adversarial testing, regression gates, and production observability.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot.
Experience in enterprise, cloud infrastructure, regulated, or mission-critical environments.
Experience in data science and applied machine learning, including classical ML techniques, deep learning models, model evaluation, and production deployment.

new_jobs.description:
Company Overview

Moss is a national privately held construction firm providing innovative solutions resulting in award-winning projects. With regional offices across the United States, Moss focuses on construction management, solar EPC, design-build, and public-private partnerships. The company’s diverse portfolio encompasses a wide range of sectors, including luxury high-rise residential, landmark mixed-use developments, hospitality, K-12 and higher education, justice, solar energy and battery storage, and sports. Moss is ranked by Engineering News-Record as one of the nation’s top 65 general contractors, and the 3rd ranked solar EPC nationwide. Moss prides itself on a strong entrepreneurial culture that honors safety, quality, client engagement and employee development. Its employees consistently rank Moss as one of the best places to work.

POSITION SCOPE AND ORGANIZATIONAL IMPACT

The Solar Director of Preconstruction and Engineering
provides leadership for preconstruction, estimating, and engineering functions to support the Solar Division in the pursuit and execution of large utility-scale solar projects
based out of the Hawaii Office
. This role drives accuracy and consistency in estimating, oversight of engineering deliverables, team development, and collaboration with owners, consultants, trade contractors, and vendors to support successful project pursuits and transitions to operations.

Essential Job Duties And Responsibilities

Lead and manage the preconstruction and engineering effort for utility-scale solar projects, from early-stage concept through final contract pricing and handoff.
Manage the estimating process for EPC, conceptual/schematic, and various stages of progress construction drawings through final contract pricing for the solar industry.
Produce estimate summaries indicating project costs and margin potential, while supporting conversion to both Owner bid forms and Moss internal budget formats.
Prepare, update, and track estimates as design documents progress, including value engineering analysis and reconciliation of scope, assumptions, and clarifications.
Provide leadership in creating, reviewing, and revising drafts and deliverables for solar utility-scale ground mount projects.
Review, analyze, and provide comments on owner contracts, subcontract agreements, consultant agreements, and other project related contracts to identify commercial, technical, operational, and risk related issues.
Build, train, and manage the preconstruction and engineering team; establish assignments, priorities, and key staff objectives.
Provide training/seminars to the department and promote continuous improvement in estimating, engineering coordination, and preconstruction processes.
Monitor adherence to all departmental processes; correct non-compliance as required.
Conduct department meetings and ensure clear communication of expectations, schedules, and deliverables.
Responsible for all deliverables produced by the department, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and timeliness.
Support and manage relationships with owners, design consultants, vendors, and trade contractors to align with project goals.
Coordinate project handoff to operations teams and ensure all preconstruction, engineering, and contractual information is accurately transferred for successful project execution
Establish and maintain strong business relationships with trade contractors and vendors to ensure support and interest in bidding and executing solar projects.
Provide support to early-stage project management, engineering, and operations teams to enable successful project planning and execution.
Communicate and interact effectively with the project owner, design consultants, and Moss staff to meet project goals.
Provide high-level summaries of bids to the Leadership Team at the time of submission or by the following morning, including key risks, assumptions, and opportunities.
Focus on risk management training and development of systems, standards, constructability, and scope development practices.
Oversee trade contractor compliance and performance expectations (including contractor scorecards) for trade contractors bidding projects.
Review trade contractor applicants who submit information through established channels and/or advise the Vice President of Solar as appropriate.
Provide staff performance reviews and recommend salary adjustments to the Vice President of Solar.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Education And Work Experience

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, electrical engineering, or related discipline preferred.
Minimum 8 years of engineering and management experience, including minimum 5 years supporting utility-scale solar projects.
Strong background in solar utility-scale ground mount projects (engineering coordination, constructability, and preconstruction execution).
Strong estimating and project scheduling background.
Strong computer skills are a necessity (MS Office / Excel / PowerPoint / Word), including familiarity with construction project management applications and estimating software.
Experience with HCSS Heavy Bid, Accubid, MS Project, Primavera, AGTEK, BlueBeam, and InSite Software is an advantage.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills required to interface directly with owners’ representatives, the A/E team, building departments, and other team members.
Ability to read, interpret, and understand plans proficiently; ability to read specifications and understand subject matter.
Ability to perform accurate quantity survey take-offs.
Demonstrated leadership skills, including experience managing and developing teams of estimators, project engineers, and/or engineering staff.

Sr Director Strategic Platform Execution

Job Summary

The Senior Director, Strategic Platform Execution leads a global organization accountable for bringing TerumoBCT's devices, disposables, and software to market. The role reports to the Senior Vice President, R&D and sits on the R&D Leadership Team. It owns how that work is planned, prioritized, sequenced, and delivered across multiple sites, along with the standards and governance that keep delivery predictable, and it is the senior R&D voice on what TerumoBCT builds and in what order. The Senior Director advises executive leadership on long-range strategy and investment, settles competing priorities, and is accountable for the results that follow, from growth in market share to lower cost and stronger product quality in developed and emerging markets. Much of that gets done through others. The functional engineering teams are peers rather than reports, so the work depends on the frameworks this role sets and on the credibility the leader builds with those teams. The same is true of Commercial, including Enterprise Marketing, where this organization is R&D's chief partner. Together they shape roadmaps, product line strategies, and value propositions, and they run Product Lifecycle Management as a shared process across functions. The Senior Director is accountable for turning what Commercial needs into commitments R&D can meet. Strategic Platform Execution is newly formed, and whoever takes it on will help decide how it is built and how TerumoBCT develops products in the years ahead. We welcome candidates who want that scope.

Essential Duties

Is the senior authority and "go to" global leader for platform, program, and project execution across the devices, disposables, and software portfolio, and represents the organization on significant matters with internal and external stakeholders
Owns planning and decision-making for the portfolio, and advises top management on long-range direction for the global platform strategy
Is the primary R&D interface to the Commercial organization, including Enterprise Marketing. Partners with them on roadmapping, product line strategies, value propositions, and cross-functional Product Lifecycle Management, and brings forward new product opportunities with a clear view of value and risk
Designs and implements frameworks for R&D operational excellence, including standard methods for project execution, resource use, performance measurement, and continuous improvement
Develops, executes, and continuously improves the organization's build, buy, and borrow competency. Sets the criteria that decide when work is insourced, outsourced, or done with a partner, and leads partner selection, integration, and ongoing governance
Establishes systematic approaches for portfolio management, resource planning, and program execution, working with the engineering functions across multiple global sites
Leads the change management and communication that carry cultural change through global R&D, and adjusts the approach based on how well it takes hold
Defines metrics and governance that track operational performance and progress on change, and that reward the way the organization wants to work
Determines the structure and staffing this organization requires, and is responsible for reviewing, evaluating, and developing its leaders and teams while working across a global, cross-functional environment
Works across regional and functional boundaries to meet business objectives and project timelines
Ensures product design and documentation meet FDA and global regulatory requirements, sets standards for technical documentation and product lifecycle management, and leads or sponsors quality system remediation and major quality initiatives
Communicates with senior management and external customers on program, strategic, and business matters, and explains complex solutions to both technical and non-technical audiences

Minimum Qualification Requirements

Education

B. S. degree in Engineering required
M.S. or PhD degree in Engineering combined with management degree preferred

Experience

Candidates will be evaluated on the depth and relevance of the following experience:

Minimum 15 years of progressive engineering experience, 10 of which have been leading engineering teams, including experience leading other people leaders
Minimum of 5 years medical device industry or equivalently regulated industry
Size and complexity of the portfolio held, measured by number of concurrent programs, annual revenue supported, and geographic footprint
Commercialized products delivered that combine devices, disposables, and software, and the candidate's specific accountability for each
Delivery through insourced, outsourced, and partnered development models, including the partners selected, the structures used, and the outcomes achieved
Scale and durability of an operating or process change the candidate led, and evidence it remained in place after their involvement ended
Direct engagement with FDA or comparable regulatory bodies, including submissions, inspections, or audits, and the candidate's role in each
Leaders developed and advanced, and the succession outcomes that followed

Skills

Credible as both a platform authority and an operational leader, setting portfolio direction while owning the discipline that delivers it
Builds R&D operating models, governance, and standards that hold up after individual programs end and leadership changes
Deep command of Design Controls and Quality Management Systems, with the standing to lead quality system remediation and defend decisions to regulators
Fluent in portfolio and program management methods, and able to apply them at global, multi-site scale
Builds and matures build, buy, and borrow capability, setting up sourcing and partnership models and strengthening them over time
Structures and governs external development relationships that hold quality, design control, intellectual property, and schedule accountability without giving up internal ownership
Sound judgment on platform trade-offs, and able to guide top management on portfolio direction, sequencing, and investment
Aligns senior stakeholders across a matrixed, consensus-driven, multi-region organization without relying on line authority
Develops senior leaders and builds succession depth for critical roles
Connects platform roadmaps to business results such as market share, cost, margin, and time to market
Uses performance data to find and close execution gaps rather than to report status
Makes trade-off decisions on scope, resources, quality, and risk with incomplete information

-Or-

An equivalent competency level acquired through a variation of these qualifications may be considered.

Physical Requirements

Typical Office Environment requirements include: reading, speaking, hearing, close vision, walking, bending, sitting, and occasional lifting up to 20 pounds.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an associate to successfully perform the essential duties of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.

new_jobs.description:
About Nscale

Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you’ll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you’ll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

About The Role

We’re hiring a Director, Supply Chain Engineering to build the systems that take Nscale from demand signal to deployed compute.

This role sits within Corporate Technology and reports to the SVP, Corporate Technology, partnering closely with Data Center and AI Infrastructure teams, as well as Finance, Procurement, and Operations. You’ll design, build, and deploy the systems, platforms, and workflows spanning demand signal, hardware configuration and BOM development, supplier and ODM coordination, logistics and staging, spare inventory management, and more. You won’t run supply chain operations or own procurement—you’ll work alongside those owners and own how the work is represented in software.

Success means this work runs on systems rather than spreadsheets. Teams will work from shared, accurate data, changes will propagate without manual chasing, and routine coordination will be handled through automation and agentic workflows. Your work will directly determine how quickly Nscale can turn hardware into live compute.

What you'll be doing

Platform Ownership & Roadmap

Own the supply chain technology stack end to end, including strategy, implementation, platform health, configuration, integrations, upgrades, and roadmap planning.
Identify capability gaps and lead the evaluation, procurement, and implementation of new tools.
Build and maintain a templated, repeatable deployment model for supply chain systems across data centers and regions.

Integration & Data Architecture

Define and govern integration architecture across supply chain, finance, procurement, logistics, and infrastructure platforms.
Ensure reliable data exchange and auditability across connected systems.
Collaboratively define the data model and maintain data integrity across platforms.
Design workflows that connect each stage of the supply chain so one team’s output becomes another team’s reliable input.

Automation & Workflow Engineering

Build systems and workflows spanning demand signals, hardware configuration, BOM development, supplier and ODM coordination, logistics, staging, and spare inventory management.
Replace spreadsheet-based processes and manual coordination with scalable systems, automation, and agentic workflows.
Ensure changes propagate across teams and systems without unnecessary manual intervention.

Stakeholder & Vendor Management

Serve as the primary technology partner for supply chain technology across Data Center, AI Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and Operations.
Manage competing demands across teams and regions while maintaining clear priorities and governance.
Own vendor relationships, contract performance, and platform renewals for purchased systems and services, applying a total-cost-of-ownership lens.
Align cross-functional stakeholders around shared standards and scalable ways of working.

KPIs

Adoption of shared systems over spreadsheet-based processes
Accuracy and integrity of cross-platform supply chain data
Reliability of integrations and change propagation
Speed from hardware demand signal to live compute

What You Must Bring

10+ years of experience in supply chain technology, enterprise systems, or a closely related field
5+ years building supply chain or supply chain adjacent technology in a complex operational environment
3+ years deploying technology systems across multiple sites or regions
Functional experience with platforms supporting to source-to-contract, BOM management, asset tracking, procure-to-pay platforms, and ERP systems
Experience in data center, hardware infrastructure, or GPU/AI compute supply chains
Proven ability to manage competing stakeholder demands while maintaining clear standards
Comfortable operating in a fast-paced evolving environment

What Sets You Apart (Preferred Qualifications)

Familiarity with DCIM/IPAM tooling and cross-border hardware logistics
Experience supporting M&A integration or global expansion from a systems perspective

What we can offer you

At Nscale, you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and we want you at the core.

Highly competitive US compensation package (base + bonus + equity), with performance reviews every 12 months.

Join one of the fastest-growing AI infrastructure companies — your chance to directly shape how global AI capacity is planned and deployed.

Expect a dynamic progression plan tailored to your ambitions. Grow by leading critical cross-functional initiatives and shaping capital strategy — always with our full support.

Human-First Flexibility: We treat you as humans first. Our flexible workplace trusts Nscalers to deliver, giving you the autonomy to shape your day around life's moments.

Equal Opportunities Statement

We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

The responsibilities outlined in this job description are not exhaustive and are intended to provide a general overview of the position. The employee may be required to perform additional duties, tasks, and responsibilities as assigned by management, consistent with the skills and qualifications required for the role.

Salary Range

In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus, equity, and/or commission programs. Nscale may offer a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, flexible paid time off, parental leave, and retirement plan participation.

new_jobs.description:
Required Qualifications (as Evidenced By An Attached Resume)

Bachelor’s degree (foreign equivalent or higher) in Engineering. Five (5) years of engineering design experience. Experience with planning, code compliance, and engineering design review. Current NYS Professional Engineer (PE) license (required for sealing and signing plans and documents). Must have, keep and maintain the appropriate valid NYS Driver’s License; have a motor vehicle record which is free from major violations or a pattern of repeat violations. (***Out-of-State Applicants, see "Special Notes”).

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree (foreign equivalent or higher). Additional years of experience with engineering design. Experience working in a large academic, healthcare, or similar setting, and project management, RFP/specification preparation and consultant coordination. Maintain industry certifications such as Revit MEP accreditation, LEED AP for green building and Certified Sustainable Building Advisor (CSBA).

Brief Description Of Duties

The Assistant Director of Engineering (MEP) provides professional engineering leadership for campus engineering design and construction administration as related to mechanical, electrical and plumbing design services for projects initial programming through the construction phase, overseeing consultant‑performed engineering services, reviewing and sealing MEP engineering plans prepared by CPDC design staff, and ensuring code‑compliant, cost‑effective solutions. The role supports RFP/RFQ development, participates in design meetings, coordinates plans and specifications, and helps maintain campus design standards. It contributes to contractor coordination, procurement review, and contract management, while supervising engineering design staff and acting for the Director of Design when assigned. The position also assists with capital project reviews, agency coordination, and special initiatives that advance campus operations and long‑term planning.

General Duties:
Assist in managing engineering services and coordination with architectural design for local projects.
Responsible for the management of the campus engineering design services contracted and performed by consultants.
Support the preparation and review of Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Request for Qualifications (RFQ’S) and consultant submissions.
Participate in design development meetings and provide technical input to senior campus officials.
Serve as a departmental representative on engineering-related matters when assigned.
Contribute to strategies that support long‑term campus goals and cost‑effective design solutions.
Oversee all engineering drawings. Review, stamp and seal plans and documents.
When assigned, assist in managing departmental operations in the absence of the Director.
Support from an engineering aspect: the oversight of construction and renovation activities, coordination with trade unions, and supervision of contractors.
Oversee the engineering design staff, including supporting performance program development, evaluations, and workload coordination.
Support labor cost estimating for the design and construction of projects.
Assist in reviewing procurement applications and payment requests related to design.
Help maintain design-related contracts and provide input on contract specifications.
Track project progress in CPR and follow up with Procurement on outstanding issues.

Plans & Specifications:
Coordinate the preparation of plans and specifications for contractor or trade union work.
Ensure preferred engineering features are incorporated into preliminary drawings.
Support the review process for working drawings and assist in preparing materials for the Director or AVP approval.

Design Standards:
Development, implementation, and maintenance of campus design standards, including mechanical, electrical and plumbing equipment, devices and fixtures.
Prepare draft plans and specifications; sealing/signing of engineering plans as required.

Special Projects:
Review capital project designs following initial planning phases.
Support coordination with SUCF, OSC, DASNY, and other agencies on design issues, scheduling, and code requirements.
Participate in special assignments such as identifying operational deficiencies and recommending improvements.
Review, stamp and sign all HSC MEP engineering drawings and documents, working with the Director of Planning, Design & Construction for HSC, architectural and engineering team for HSC.
Assist and review grant programs and designs with the Director of Special Initiatives and Grant Management.

Other duties or projects as assigned as appropriate to rank and departmental mission.

Special Notes

This is a full-time appointment. FLSA Exempt position, not eligible for the overtime provisions of the FLSA. Minimum salary threshold must be met to maintain FLSA exemption.

In addition to the employee's base salary, this position is eligible for $4,000 UUP annual location pay, paid biweekly.

Essential Position:
This has been designated as an essential position based on the duties of the job and the functions performed. Positions that are designated as such may be required to report to work/remain at work even if classes are canceled, and the campus is working on limited operations in an emergency.

Out-of-State Applicants: Please note as a condition of employment and in order for this position to be tendered, the successful incumbent will be required to provide evidence of a valid license and driving abstract from the state issuing the license within five business days of a conditional offer and must obtain a NYS driver's license within 30 days of start date.

For this position, we are unable to sponsor candidates for work visas.

Job Description

Joining Amex Tech means discovering and shaping your contribution to something big. Here, you can work alongside talented tech teams and build a unique career with the Powerful Backing of American Express. With a range of opportunities to work with the latest technologies, and a commitment to back the broader engineering community through open source, our mission is to power your success. Because Amex Tech is powered by our technology, our culture, and our colleagues.

The Technology organization enables and accelerates the company’s growth strategies, delivering global capabilities and services in support of Amex’s customers and colleagues, while maintaining 24/7 servicing and availability to ensure an uninterrupted, high-quality customer experience. Technology provides the foundation for everything we do in the company while driving differentiation through building and leveraging innovative technology and data insights.

The Enterprise Technology Services organization partners with every part of the American Express business to power the company’s growth and innovation with trust and efficiency, and drive competitive differentiation with speed. We support the delivery and operations of technology, digital, and data capabilities, platforms, and services globally. Specifically, our team is responsible for the company’s technology engineering, architecture, and infrastructure, providing 24x7 support to ensure an uninterrupted, high-quality experience for customers and colleagues. We also provide product management for core enterprise platforms, and lead technology risk and information security, enterprise data governance and platforms, digital product and design, and enterprise AI platforms on behalf of the company.

The Global Risk & Compliance Technology (GRCT) organization protects Amex with 2nd and 3rd lines of defense systems for Financial Crimes Risk Management and Integrated Risk Management to build a world-class risk-management framework that empowers colleagues to make informed, secure growth decisions, which fosters a trusted brand.

Responsibilities

Team Leadership:

Lead, mentor, and manage a team of engineers, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Provide technology guidance and career development support to team members.

Project Management

Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of engineering projects, ensuring they meet quality, budget, and timeline requirements.
Collaborate with partners to define project details, objectives, and outcomes.

Technology Expertise

Drive phased and iterative improvement journeys from all angles of People, Processes/Practices and Technologies involved.
Review and approve designs, architecture, and code to maintain high standards.
Undertake Tech modernization journeys to Industry latest/greatest.
Manage and support end-to-end technology-landscape for Risk Management systems and Products, specifically on Financial Crimes Compliance.
Build integrated Product roadmaps and strategies.

Collaboration

Work closely with product owners, business process owners, and other stakeholders to align engineering efforts with business objectives.
Communicate progress, risks, and solutions to partners effectively.
Process Improvement:
Identify and implement standard processes, tools, and methodologies to optimize engineering workflows.
Ensure compliance with industry standards, security protocols, and regulatory requirements.
Applies visualization and other techniques to fast track concepts
Functions as a core member of an Agile team driving User story analysis & elaboration, design and development of software applications, testing & builds automation tools
Works on a specific platform/product assigned to projects based on demand and business priority
Sees opportunities to adopt innovative technologies
Embodies “rebel with a cause” mentality by looking beyond the obvious for continuous improvement opportunities.
Support Global Risk and Compliance delivery team to lead and assist in the design and actual development of applications.
Responsible for specific functional areas within the team, this involves project management and taking business specifications.
The individual should be able to independently run projects/tasks delegated to him.
Develop and maintain project related documentation,
Provide system support and user support/training/communication for implemented applications.

Qualifications

Bachelor degree in Engineering or Computer Science or equivalent OR Master’s in Computer Applications or equivalent.
10 to 14 years of experience is required.
Expert in Cloud Technologies (GCP, AWS, etc).
Expert in System Design.
Experience with managing e2e software-delivery for integrating with vendor-systems (SaaS/COTS).
Experience with managing e2e software delivery for building complex real-time cloud-native/hybrid distributed systems.
Experience with managing continuous software delivery for live business-as-usual high-stakes Production systems.
Experience in process automation.
Experience in distributed programming.
Experience in analysis, design, development, testing, and implementation of data applications.
Demonstrated ability to develop and document specifications and analyze software and system processing flows.
Creative problem solving (Innovative) and strategic critical thinking.
Experience of delivery using Agile Methodologies.
Experience of defining and using CI/CD pipelines.

At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and service.

As part of Team Amex, you’ll experience our powerful backing with comprehensive support for your holistic well-being and many opportunities to learn new skills, develop as a leader, and grow your career.
